item.title: Credit Corporation Fiji strengthens it’s presence with new Nakasi office and permanent Labasa home
item.description: Credit Corporation (Fiji) Pte Limited (CCFL) has strengthened its presence across Fiji with the relocation of its Nakasi branch to new, larger premises at Tebara Complex and the acquisition of the strata unit housing its Labasa branch at Damodar Complex. The two milestones reflect CCFL’s continued commitment to investing in its customers, its people and the communities it serves across Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
Credit Corporation (Fiji) Pte Limited (CCFL) has strengthened its presence across Fiji with the relocation of its Nakasi branch to new, larger premises at Tebara Complex and the acquisition of the strata unit housing its Labasa branch at Damodar Complex.

The two milestones reflect CCFL’s continued commitment to investing in its customers, its people and the communities it serves across Fiji.

CCFL has relocated its Nakasi branch to the left wing of Tebara Complex, providing customers with a significantly larger and more modern office designed to support the branch’s continued growth.

The new premises provide additional space for customer service, private consultations and staff, enabling CCFL to deliver a more comfortable and efficient experience for customers while supporting the branch’s growing operations.

The Nakasi office will also serve as an important Business Continuity Planning (BCP) site supporting CCFL’s operations in Suva.

CCFL has also acquired the strata unit housing its Labasa branch at Damodar Complex, establishing a permanent home for its operations in the Northern Division.

Since establishing its presence in Labasa in June 2024, CCFL has experienced strong growth in its customer base, particularly among small and medium-sized enterprises.

The acquisition reinforces CCFL’s long-term commitment to the Northern market and provides a strong foundation from which the company can continue to support customers and businesses across Vanua Levu, including Savusavu and Taveuni.

“Our customers are at the centre of every decision we make. The relocation of our Nakasi branch gives us the space and environment to provide an even better experience for our growing customer base, while our acquisition of the Labasa premises demonstrates our long-term commitment to the North. As Credit Corporation Fiji continues to grow, we remain focused on being accessible to our customers, delivering quality service and investing in the communities and markets where we operate.” Mohammed Nawaz, Country Manager, CCFL.

CCFL continues to strengthen its footprint across Fiji through investments that improve customer service, operational resilience and access to finance for individuals and businesses.

The company remains committed to supporting the growth of both established and emerging markets throughout Fiji.

item.title: Fresh psychiatric assessment ordered for teen accused in Waimanu Road killing
item.description: The High Court in Suva has granted a one-month adjournment for an independent doctor to complete a psychiatric assessment on former high school student Rihaal Kumar, who is accused of a fatal stabbing on Waimanu Road. Mr Kumar’s lawyer sought the time in court today to allow the medical expert to complete the evaluation and compile a report.
item.content:encoded:
The High Court in Suva has granted a one-month adjournment for an independent doctor to complete a psychiatric assessment on former high school student Rihaal Kumar, who is accused of a fatal stabbing on Waimanu Road.

Mr Kumar’s lawyer sought the time in court today to allow the medical expert to complete the evaluation and compile a report.

The application follows two previous psychiatric reports which found the accused unfit to enter a plea or stand trial.

The prosecution alleges that the killing was premeditated, claiming that five days before the incident, the teenager purchased a $5 dagger and asked his father to sharpen it.

Mr Kumar is alleged to have used the dagger along with two kitchen knives to stab Sharuf Shaakir Khan multiple times in the stomach, thigh, and back at an apartment complex on Waimanu Road in Suva on July 7, 2025.

The deceased’s body was discovered by his brother-in-law, after which Kumar allegedly admitted to the killing before police were alerted.

Justice Daniel Goundar adjourned the matter to November 6, 2026, for the independent psychiatric report to be furnished to the court.

Mr Kumar has been further remanded under the care of Saint Giles Hospital.

item.title: Kumar appeal adjourned as defence raises trial lawyer incompetence
item.description: THE Court of Appeal in Suva has adjourned the criminal appeal hearing of Kusal Kunal Kumar after his defence team sought to introduce fresh evidence alleging incompetence against his trial lawyer, Mr J Reddy. The matter, originating from Labasa High Court Case No. HAC 16 of 2022, was set down for hearing on September 8 and ruled the day after before Justices of Appeal Chandana Prematilaka, Pamela
item.content:encoded:
THE Court of Appeal in Suva has adjourned the criminal appeal hearing of Kusal Kunal Kumar after his defence team sought to introduce fresh evidence alleging incompetence against his trial lawyer, Mr J Reddy.

The matter, originating from Labasa High Court Case No. HAC 16 of 2022, was set down for hearing on September 8 and ruled the day after before Justices of Appeal Chandana Prematilaka, Pamela Andrews, and Robert Dobson.

Appellant’s lawyer, Abhay Singh, advised the court that he filed a motion for leave to adduce fresh evidence supported by affidavits making allegations against Kumar’s former trial lawyer.

Mr Singh stated that if the application was allowed, he intended to amend the grounds of appeal to include “counsel incompetence”.

However, the Court noted that mandatory procedures outlined in the precedent case Nilesh Chand v State had not been followed. Under the set procedure, the Court Registrar must serve the application, supporting affidavits, and a waiver of privilege directly to the former lawyer to allow them an opportunity to respond.

Finding that the court file contained no evidence of formal service or response from Reddy, the bench ruled that it was inappropriate to hear the application or the substantive appeal until Mr Reddy was given an opportunity to reply.

The Court ordered Mr Singh to file any additional material regarding former counsel’s conduct within seven days. The Registrar has been directed to forward the application and materials to Mr Reddy, who will have three weeks to file a response by way of affidavit.

The appellant will subsequently have two weeks to reply to the response.

The Court of Appeal has adjourned the hearing and directed the matter to be listed for further steps in January 2027 before the President of the Court of Appeal.

Kumar was represented by A.K. Singh Lawyers, while Luisa Latu appeared for the State.

item.title: Youth under community supervision
item.description: A HIGH Court judge in Labasa has warned a youth that using a caneknife handle to poke a female classmate between her legs was totally unacceptable before placing him under community supervision. The warning was issued by Justice Lee James Burney to an 18-year-old who appeared for sentencing after being acquitted of rape but convicted of the lesser offence of indecent assault.
item.content:encoded:
A HIGH Court judge in Labasa has warned a youth that using a caneknife handle to poke a female classmate between her legs was totally unacceptable before placing him under community supervision.

The warning was issued by Justice Lee James Burney to an 18-year-old who appeared for sentencing after being acquitted of rape but convicted of the lesser offence of indecent assault.

The court found that on February 22, 2024, the teenager deliberately poked his schoolmate while they were returning garden tools after an agricultural practical lesson.

Both individuals were 16 years old at the time of the incident.

Justice Burney told the youth that it was very important to learn his lesson at a young age, warning him that failing to do so could risk throwing away his promising future.

A thorough pre-sentence report revealed that the teenager lives with his parents in a supportive environment, enjoys school, and aspires to become a boat captain.

item.title: Trust funds developments
item.description: ABOUT 10 per cent of passenger fares paid by guests travelling on South Sea Cruises’ Yasawa Princess 2 is directed to the Vinaka Fiji Trust for community development projects in the Yasawa Islands. Vinaka Fiji coordinator Samisoni Ulitu said the organisation worked with the Ba Provincial Office, village development plans, and individual village requests to determine which communities required assi
item.content:encoded:
ABOUT 10 per cent of passenger fares paid by guests travelling on South Sea Cruises’ Yasawa Princess 2 is directed to the Vinaka Fiji Trust for community development projects in the Yasawa Islands.

Vinaka Fiji coordinator Samisoni Ulitu said the organisation worked with the Ba Provincial Office, village development plans, and individual village requests to determine which communities required assistance.

“We work with the provincial office, data from village development plans and requests that are made to our office,” he said.

Vinaka Fiji supports projects aimed at improving basic services and facilities, including water tanks, rainwater harvesting systems, solar lighting, school repairs, and community halls.

Mr Ulitu said the program was funded partly through contributions from visitors’ boat fares.

“It’s taken from our Yasawa Princess 2 guests, usually 10 per cent of their passenger fares,” he said, adding that financial transparency reports can be accessed through their finance team.

Mr Ulitu said local communities also contribute manpower towards projects.

He said water tanks installed under rain-harvesting projects were constructed to withstand tropical cyclones.

“The water tanks are constructed in a more structured way to withstand disasters such as hurricanes. Tanks are anchored, while gutters are secured with clips.”

Mr Ulitu said Vinaka Fiji also supports education and employment initiatives.

item.title: Cousins avoid jail time
item.description: TWO teenage cousins, who broke into a relative’s Nadi home on December 30, 2025, and stole a television, clothes, and bags walked away from the High Court in Lautoka with suspended sentences. Justice Aruna Aluthge sentenced the two on August 31 ordering names to be suppressed because they were juveniles at the time of the offences.
item.content:encoded:
TWO teenage cousins, who broke into a relative’s Nadi home on December 30, 2025, and stole a television, clothes, and bags walked away from the High Court in Lautoka with suspended sentences.

Justice Aruna Aluthge sentenced the two on August 31 ordering names to be suppressed because they were juveniles at the time of the offences.

Each received a two-year prison term, suspended for three years.

The teenagers will be placed on probation under the supervision of a welfare officer.

Further offences committed during the suspension period will result in the two serving the original sentence behind bars.

The juveniles targeted the couple’s home in Nadi while they were away during the day.

They gained entry by opening a sitting room window grill and neighbouring children spotted the pair inside the house.

When the owners returned to find their bedroom ransacked and property missing, the man traced a trail nearby and recovered the stolen 32-inch television wrapped in garbage bags, along with the remaining stolen clothing items.

Both youths voluntarily surrendered to Nadi police, admitted the offences during caution interviews, and pleaded guilty at the earliest opportunity.

While burglaries are on the rise in Fiji,Justice Aluthge said, the offence fell into the lower harm category as the stolen property was of minimal value and the opportunistic theft involved no violence.

He said young and first-time offenders deserved an opportunity to rehabilitate.

He said special circumstances, including one of the juvenile’s studies in cookery at Fiji National University, their genuine remorse, full recovery of the stolen goods, and clean records, justified suspending the prison term.
